keyVerseText: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes. grapes: Gr. a grape
rootMeaning: The Greek verb τρυγάω (trygáō) derives from a root related to τρύγω, meaning 'to dry,' which metaphorically points to ripe fruit as if it were dried and ready for harvest. This etymology enriches the common English gloss 'gather' by emphasizing the act of collecting fruit at its proper season of ripeness, highlighting a process of careful selection and timing rather than a general collection.
usageInScripture: τρυγάω appears three times in the New Testament, consistently translated with the sense of 'gather' or 'gathered.' This usage reflects both the literal act of harvesting fruit and a metaphorical sense of collecting or reaping from a source. The translations 'gather they,' 'gather,' and 'gathered' reveal a focus on the deliberate action of bringing in what has matured or is ready, underscoring the word's agricultural and symbolic significance.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding τρυγάω as the gathering of ripe fruit deepens our appreciation of biblical imagery related to spiritual harvest and judgment. The concept of gathering at the right time aligns with God's sovereign timing in bringing forth fruit from believers' lives and in executing divine justice. This verb reminds Christians that faith and works mature over time and that God evaluates the 'fruit' produced, both in character and actions. In Christ-centered theology, it underscores the call to bear lasting fruit that will be gathered into God's kingdom, reflecting a life transformed by grace.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 6:44 states, 'For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.' Here, τρυγάω conveys the intentional gathering of fruit that reveals the true nature of the tree. The word highlights the principle that genuine fruit—spiritual or moral—cannot be falsely produced or collected from an unworthy source, emphasizing discernment and authenticity in the Christian life.
